newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Jet fuel trades lower at $25/bbl.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Jet fuel trades lower at $25/bbl.

text.p: Singapore's physical jet fuel was traded lower on Monday at $25.00 per barrel, down 15 cents from its last traded level a week ago, underlining the current softness of the market, traders said.
The physical deal underscored the sliding swaps jet/gas oil regrade, with prompt-month June trading for the first time at minus 10 cents and was quoted in the range of minus 10 and minus 30 cents.

Traders said the 100,000-barrel physical parcel was bought by a Singapore trader from a European major for June 14-18 lifting, amid soft regional demand as buyers no longer buying in large volumes to prop up prices.
"We see little if any demand for jet in the region now," one trader said.
Gas oil was steady amid abundant offers with seven sellers offering 10 cargoes for June between $25.60 and $25.80 per barrel free-on-board basis.
Only two buyers emerged with four bids around $25.40 per barrel, but nothing was traded.

Traders said a US major recently bought 30,000 tonnes of gas oil from a South Korean refiner at $1.05 per barrel premium to Singapore spot quotes, for end-May/early June delivery cost-and-freight Hong Kong.
Traders said they expect premiums into Hong Kong to slip in the near term.
They also said that a 80,000-tonne cargo of 0.5-percent sulphur gas oil was sold recently at 30 cents per barrel over MidEast quotes, free-on-board Ruwais.
Traders said the premium was very attractive in the light of current seasonal slowdown in demand which are forcing MidEast premiums to narrow from around 35 cents.
Traders said result of the Abu Dhabi National Oil Co (ADNOC) gas oil sale tender for 75,000 tonnes remained hazy with aggressive bids seen between 35 and 40 cents per barrel above MidEast quotes.
